framing: Nobody ships pure free strings with no list anywhere, and nobody ships pure rows with no free text. Hybrid is modal, and in every case the hybrid is governed by a flag or kind on the definition — #10778 V2 exactly. The one thing no platform does: keep one shared definition and give it a different value list per category. GS1 (netContent is a QuantitativeValue because a measurement without a unitCode is not interpretable across trading partners) and BPOM/Kemendag (the printed unit is a function of the magnitude) carry the only stated rationale for a typed quantity.

rows.h: copied; the shared-vocabulary half is ❓UNKNOWN (U16); quantities: five shapes at once
rows.shape: “name is stable; the label is not.” The value is a scalar inside an array-of-objects envelope written onto the child: [{ "value": 4, "marketplace_id": "ATVPDKIKX0DER" }]. Whether Flavor, flavor.value_id and Flavor Standardized Values are three attributes or three views of one is not established. The enum lives inside the per-(ProductType, marketplace) schema and is soft: a free string is schema-valid, a suggested closed list sits alongside. Quantities: {value, unit}, unit_count {value, type}, a bare integer and free-text size ≤50 chars in one schema. Amazon staff on the enum-vs-validator mismatch: “getDefinitionsProductType publishes human-readable display values in enum/enumNames … while the server-side validator only accepts undocumented snake_case codes … a valid concern.”

rows.h: hybrid split by option kind, not attribute type; list on the attribute (taxonomy) / category (linked) / product (unlinked)
rows.shape: “An unlinked option value is a string on the product … A linked option value carries linkedMetafieldValue: "gid://shopify/Metaobject/253676454209" — a reference to a Metaobject row that exists independently of the product; two products linked to the same metaobject each read back the same gid.” Unlinked, measured live: 600 products → 600 distinct ProductOptionValue ids for one value name. Taxonomy values: a TaxonomyValue belongs to exactly one attribute (0 of 74,820 shared). Metafield values are always stored as a string regardless of type. Quantities: weight and unit-price on the variant; a measurement attribute type exists in the taxonomy, 0 instances across 383 nodes. The clearest stated “why” for a shared row — the rename argument: “instead of a color option with the text value ‘Red’, you reference a metaobject that includes the color name, hex code, and taxonomy references … you can edit the color black to be graphite and your variant values are updated anywhere that color is used.” Live 2026-09-21: 16 categories → 99 TaxonomyChoiceListAttribute (values are TaxonomyValue {id: ID!, name: String!} rows) and 0 TaxonomyMeasurementAttribute; the measurement type's options introspect as [Attribute {key: String!, value: String}] — bare strings, no unit field.

rows.h: every value is a string on the product; quantities are text + a unit-pricing pair
rows.shape: Four open layers where the merchant names the key and writes a free string, plus one typed layer: ProductDetail {sectionName, attributeName, attributeValue} (140/140/1000 chars, ≤100); CustomAttribute {name, value} (≤2,500 per product); VariantOption {name, value} (0..30; name free text ≤250, no enumeration); CloudExportAdditionalProperties. Flavour is only a suggested key name in product_detail — “not a comprehensive or exhaustive list.” Quantities: “Value + unit” packed into one feed string; unit_pricing_measure / unit_pricing_base_measure beside it; no dedicated net-content field. Inference: feeds from merchants whose catalogues Google does not host — no place a shared row could live that both sides can address.

rows.h: copied; typed on the constraint, no physical unit; FREE_TEXT on 156,337 of 197,046
rows.shape: aspects = {name: [strings]} on each SKU; “There is no identifier on an aspect or an aspect value” (0 hits for aspectId, valueId, aspectValueId over 867 MB). The list lives on the leaf category (the same id under two trees returns two different lists). Data type on the constraint (NUMBER 482 / DATE 15 of 197,046); every value is a string. Why free text coexists with a closed list, in the vendor's words: “Most categories support free-text names and values in item specifics and in variations. However, some categories require certain item specifics (e.g., Brand), and some item specifics (e.g., Color) may require you to select a value from a predefined set.”

rows.h: copied; typed {unit, measure} on netContent; flavor never closed
rows.shape: “The axis value is copied per item; there is no shared value row — written inline on each member ("flavor":"Peppermint" / "Spearmint")”; “Shared values are shared by repetition, not reference.” The list is written out per product type — but for flavor all 385 declarations are "type":"string", maxLength 600, no enum: 0 of 6,967 types close it. Quantities: {unit, measure} objects on values like netContent; the axis-eligible size stays a free string. Inference: a flat feed contract — the seller transmits a complete document per SKU, and Walmart never hands the seller an id to point at.

rows.h: shared row by id, or the sentinel 0 + free text; typed value carries a unit
rows.shape: value_id int on the catalogue row (attribute 1 : N); value_id int32 required on the item with 0 = custom sentinel (“‘value_id’ must be 0 and ‘original_value_name’ is required”). List on the attribute: search_attribute_value_list keyed by attribute_id alone. Quantities: value_unit when the attribute's format_type = 2, unit from the attribute's own attribute_unit_list (name = “5kg”, value_unit = the unit); variation options are bare. Inference: a marketplace that wants a clean catalogue but cannot block a seller's listing.

rows.h: both eras hybrid; Era A bare, Era B typed quantity via a product attribute + a unit-price formula
rows.shape: Era A: VariantUnitValue {variant_unit_value_id int, status int, value string, equivalent_value_id int, english_value string, hex string, icon string} — a value row per variant unit; “To create a custom variant simply fill value with desired value.” No unit field. Era B: id string ← built-in attribute id, value_id string ← built-in value id (from Get Attributes), beside a seller-typed custom attribute whose “system will auto-generate an ID after listing.” Quantity: skus.sku_unit_count pairs a magnitude on the SKU with “base unit count” and “unit type” product attributes served by Get Attributes — “if the SKU represents 500ml of water, this value would be 500 if the unit type is defined as ml” — and the only stated unit-price formula in the set: “Unit price = Selling price / (SKU unit count / base unit count).” Structured spec 2026-09-21: a product-attribute value is written as {id, name}, a sales-attribute value as {id, value_id, value_name, name} — id-bearing row or a name, the hybrid stated in the schema; every money and quantity field is a string.

rows.h: shared row; list on the option; unit on the variation
rows.shape: CatalogItemOptionValue is a top-level catalog object with its own id; a variation stores {"item_option_id", "item_option_value_id"} pairs. Vendor: “that option can be applied to define the color attribute for any new catalog items”; “because ‘Polo shirt’ and ‘Club shirt’ are variations of ‘Shirt’, they're restricted to the same option values. If the seller later receives teal polo shirts, they must add ‘Teal’ to the color option set.” Custom-attribute values, by contrast, are inline (string_value / number_value / boolean_value / selection_uid_values). Quantity: the variation points at a CatalogMeasurementUnit.

rows.h: local vs shared is a first-class choice; no retrieved instance data (U9)
rows.shape: The import XSD offers variation-attribute (inline, own values) or shared-variation-attribute (a reference carrying only attribute-id + variation-attribute-id); the object carries shared: boolean. The value is @value (NonEmptyString.256, 1..1 required, e.g. red, 1 GB) with <display-value> localized 0..N and position (Data API only). Quantities: 1 GB is one opaque string; the unit sits on the definition (unit: String) and the product (unit-quantity xsd:decimal, unit-measure String.60). Provenance caveat: two artifacts labelled “REAL INSTANCE” are vendor-authored examples.

rows.h: shared row at the definition, copied code at the product; metric is {amount, unit} and axis-eligible
rows.shape: “The definition is a shared row; the product copies the code.” pim_catalog_attribute_option UNIQUE (code, attribute_id), labels in pim_catalog_attribute_option_value (locale_code, option_id); the product stores the option code as a string inside raw_values JSON. “Referential integrity is a validator, not a foreign key” — case-insensitive: in_array(strtolower($value->getData()), …). AttributeOption.attribute manyToOne, exactly 1; no family/category field. Quantity: pim_catalog_metric = {amount, unit} from a shared unit registry ({"amount":"800.0000","unit":"GRAM","symbol":"g"}, symbol resolved from the measurement family), and it is axis-eligible. Ordering, both mechanisms stated: “Options can be automatically sorted by alphabetical order using the toggle button … you can manually drag and drop option rows to reorder.”

rows.h: shared term for the attribute, copied slug for the axis; bare, nothing
rows.shape: “The attribute value is a bare label — id (integer, readonly), name, slug, description, menu_order (integer), count”, but “A variation stores its axis value as a copied string, always, even for a global attribute” — update_post_meta($product_id, 'attribute_' . $key, wp_slash($value)). Global terms on the attribute; local attributes on the product only. Quantities: six bare fields; numeric sort is an ORDER BY name+0 hack (attribute_orderby = name_num). The only explicit global-vs-local trade statement: “defined globally, so they’re easy to update across the entire store … or defined individually, at the product level.”

rows.h: the record withdrew its own “copied, not a foreign key” reading; typed, no physical unit
rows.shape: AttributePlainEnumValue {key: string, label: string} — a pair nested inside the ProductType document, not an addressable row. 13 attribute types; money carries a currency, not a unit; no unit fields (four instruments, all 0). (B) on both: “the enum values can be different for each ProductType” while “each AttributeDefinition must have the same type.” Why values differ per type: “You wouldn't ask for the Neckline of a pair of jeans, would you?”

rows.h: shared row referenced by integer; list on the attribute; bare, nothing
rows.shape: “The value is a shared row referenced by an integer, not a string copied onto each product; the label is fanned out per store view, never per product.” eav_attribute_option (option_id) → eav_attribute_option_value (value_id, option_id, store_id, value varchar(255)), UNIQUE (store_id, option_id); the product stores catalog_product_entity_int.value (int). The running store holds the union of two fixtures' size lists (20 options). Quantities: 0 unit fields across 67 schema files (control 12). Inference for the row: labels are per store_id, so the label cannot be the identity — a store-view translation of “Green” must not create a second value.
